title: Book 8 — Urania, Chapter 123
paragraphs: After the division of the spoils, the Greeks sailed to the Isthmus to award the prize of valor to the Greek who had proved himself most worthy in this war. When they had come there, and the commanders cast their votes at the altar of Poseidon, choosing from the whole number the first and the second in merit, each man voted for himself, thinking he had been the best; but for the second place the majority of votes agreed, going to Themistocles. So while the others were left alone in their own votes, Themistocles far surpassed them all in the second-place voting.
